summary: This bill requires the Inspector General of the Department of Health and Human Services to submit quarterly reports to Congress for two years detailing investigations, prosecutions, alleged fraud amounts, charges, and exclusions related to Medicare and Medicaid fraud.

scores.thoughts: This bill focuses on reporting Medicare and Medicaid fraud, which are public healthcare programs. By seeking to identify and reduce fraud, it aims to improve the efficiency and integrity of these public systems, thus strengthening public healthcare.

Medicare and Medicaid are significant components of the social safety net, providing healthcare to vulnerable populations. By addressing fraud within these programs, the bill indirectly supports the sustainability and effectiveness of this safety net, preventing the erosion of funds intended for beneficiaries.

The bill requires regular HHS IG reports detailing Medicare and Medicaid fraud investigations, prosecutions, dollar amounts, and exclusions, with the explicit goal of recovering misspent funds. This directly targets waste in two of the largest federal entitlement programs and is the sole purpose of the legislation, making deficit reduction through reduced improper payments central to the bill.

The legislation mandates ongoing government oversight and reporting on fraud within Medicare and Medicaid, two major public insurance programs, to curb improper expenditures. This constitutes government action aimed at lowering program costs rather than relying on market competition or reduced federal involvement.
